title: Evaluation of skeletal age based on Greulich-Pyle method in Tehran
author: Ebrahimzade, Rahban, et al.
materials: The aim of this methodology is to determine the differences between bone age and chronological age in Iranian children which could lead more accurate estimation of bone age. To compare bone age with chronological age, 40 children were randomly selected. Subjects aged between 2 and 18 years living in Tehran City, Iran. Exclusion criteria were history of systemic diseases more than 1 month, history of chronic systemic diseases, history of hospitalization for more than a week, and people with height or weight above the percentile of 97% or below 3 percent percentile. After receiving informed consent from patients and their parents, radiograph of the left wrist and hand was taken. Based on GP [5], all radiographs were reported by a radiologist who was of the patient’s chronological age. These individuals were divided into four groups: 2–5.99, 6–9.99, 10–13.99 and 14–18 years old.

steps.title: Select study participants
steps.instruction: Randomly select 40 children aged 2 to 18 years living in Tehran, Iran.

steps.title: Apply exclusion criteria
steps.instruction: Exclude any child with a history of systemic disease lasting more than 1 month, any chronic systemic disease, hospitalization longer than 1 week, or height or weight above the 97th percentile or below the 3rd percentile.

steps.title: Obtain informed consent
steps.instruction: After receiving written informed consent from each child’s parents (or legal guardians) and assent from the child when appropriate, proceed to data collection.

steps.title: Acquire left‑hand radiograph
steps.instruction: Take a standard radiograph of the left wrist and hand for each enrolled child.

steps.title: Determine bone age
steps.instruction: Have a radiologist, blinded to the child’s chronological age, evaluate each radiograph using the Greulich‑Pyle (GP) atlas and record the bone age.

steps.title: Record anthropometric data
steps.instruction: For each child, record chronological age (years), weight (kg), height (cm), and calculate Body Mass Index (BMI = kg/m²).

steps.title: Classify by age and BMI groups
steps.instruction: Assign each child to one of four chronological age groups (2–5.99, 6–9.99, 10–13.99, 14–18 years) and to one of four BMI categories (<18.5, 18.5–24.9, 25–29.9, ≥30).

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Using SPSS, check normality of each variable with the Shapiro–Wilk test; then for each age‑BMI subgroup calculate mean ± SD of bone age, chronological age, weight, height, and BMI; finally compare bone age to chronological age with a One‑Sample T‑Test.
